newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament drops demand for ban on U.S. programs.
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament drops demand for ban on U.S. programs.

text.p: The European Parliament Tuesday abandoned its long-standing demands for stricter limits on the number of Hollywood programmes on European television, sidestepping a showdown with European governments.

Although a majority of members demanded that a rule requiring 51 percent of Europe's TV programmes be European be made mandatory, the proposal failed to secure the majority needed to force EU governments to negotiate on the issue.

The vote brings to an end one of the EU's longest-running sagas, surrounding the EU's 1989 "television without borders" directive, which members had hoped to use to break Hollywood's domination of the EU's television screens.
The parliament had effectively been fighting a losing battle with EU culture ministers, who had made clear in advance they had no intention of curbing the prime U.S. export industry.
